definitions.explanation: Passing through an intermediate point on the way to a destination.

examples.japanese: {大阪|おおさか}{経由|けいゆ}で{東京|とうきょう}へ{行|い}く。
examples.english: To go to Tokyo via Osaka.

examples.japanese: {成田|なりた}{空港|くうこう}{経由|けいゆ}
{友人|ゆうじん}を{経由|けいゆ}して{連絡|れんらく}した。
examples.english: I contacted them through a friend.

examples.japanese: この{荷物|にもつ}は{香港|ほんこん}を{経由|けいゆ}して{届|とど}けられたので、{配送|はいそう}に{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: This package was delivered via Hong Kong, so shipping took a long time.

notes:
{経由|けいゆ} means passing through an intermediate point on the way to a final destination. It can describe physical routes, communication channels, or abstract processes.

TWO GRAMMATICAL PATTERNS:
- 〜{経由|けいゆ}で: noun modifier (no particle before {経由|けいゆ}), e.g. {大阪|おおさか}{経由|けいゆ}で{東京|とうきょう}へ
- 〜を{経由|けいゆ}して: verb pattern with を, e.g. {香港|ほんこん}を{経由|けいゆ}して{届|とど}く

USAGE DOMAINS:
- Travel/transport: {成田|なりた}{経由|けいゆ}の{便|びん} (flight via Narita)
- Communication: {友人|ゆうじん}を{経由|けいゆ}して{連絡|れんらく}する (contact through a friend)
- Technology: サーバーを{経由|けいゆ}する (go through a server)

CONTRAST:
- {経由|けいゆ}: emphasizes passing through a point along the way
- {通|とお}って: more casual, simply means "going through"
- {経|へ}て: more literary, emphasizes a process or passage of time
